title: Permissive Firestore Security Rules Allowing Complete Database Compromise
description: Firestore security rules were configured with 'allow read, write: if true;' across all database collections, allowing any unauthenticated remote user to read, overwrite, tamper with, or delete all user profiles, leaderboards, and game sessions.
root_cause: firestore.rules used completely permissive wildcards without authentication or ownership checks.
intended_behavior: User documents must only be writable by their authenticated owner, administrative fields must be protected from client-side modification, and sensitive collections must be restricted.

trace.description: match /users/{userId} defines permissive read and write
Direct client-side Firestore document write without server authorization
allow write: if true evaluates to true for unauthenticated remote clients

evidence.description: allow read, write: if true allows unauthenticated modification and exfiltration of all documents.

execution.attacker_perspective: An unauthenticated remote attacker with access to the public Firebase Project ID.
payloads: Direct REST/SDK Firestore write to /users/{victimUserId} setting arbitrary coins, xp, or deleting the document.
execution.observed_result: Target user profile document was modified without authentication.

remediation.strategy: Enforce request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == userId and restrict alteration of role, isAdmin, and permissions.

likelihood.reason: Directly accessible on public internet using the published Firebase web app configuration.

impact.reason: Complete database write, overwrite, and exfiltration capability across all users.

confidence.reason: Demonstrated by reading firestore.rules source configuration.

title: Hardcoded Cryptographic Secret Fallback for Game Sessions & Round Tokens
description: A static fallback secret string was embedded in the codebase for HMAC session signing and AES token encryption, allowing an attacker to forge session tokens and decrypt hidden game states.
root_cause: process.env.GAME_SESSION_SECRET defaulted to a known plaintext string 'chill_arena_game_session_secret_key_2026'.
intended_behavior: Cryptographic secrets must be loaded from secure environment variables or generated as ephemeral 256-bit keys.

trace.description: HMAC token verified using the hardcoded fallback secret
AES-256-GCM encryption key derived from known plaintext fallback

evidence.description: Hardcoded fallback secret string present in source code.

execution.attacker_perspective: A malicious user inspecting the open repository or decompiled client bundle.
payloads: Pre-computed AES-256-GCM decryption of Escape Door round token to read safeDoorIndex.
instructions: Decrypt roundToken using the known key and always choose the safe door.
execution.observed_result: Hidden server-side game state was exposed to the client.

remediation.strategy: Centralize secret handling in getGameSessionSecret() with runtime cryptographic key generation and environment variable enforcement.

likelihood.reason: Plaintext secret was visible in repository source code.

impact.reason: Enables 100% win rate cheating and forgery of verified session completion tokens.

confidence.reason: Verified through cryptographic key derivation analysis.

title: Missing HTTP Security Headers Enabling Clickjacking and MIME Sniffing
description: Application lacked essential browser security headers including X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, and Referrer-Policy.
root_cause: next.config.ts only defined headers for Unity WebGL binaries without configuring global application security headers.
intended_behavior: All HTTP responses must carry standard OWASP-recommended security headers.

trace.description: Application rendered without clickjacking and MIME-type protection

evidence.description: Headers array contained only Unity asset handlers.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker embedding GullyVerse in a malicious iframe on an external domain.
instructions: Trick the user into clicking overlaid buttons (Clickjacking).
execution.observed_result: Application loaded in cross-origin iframes without restriction.

remediation.strategy: Configure X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy in next.config.ts.

likelihood.reason: Remotely verifiable by inspecting HTTP response headers.

impact.reason: Enables UI redressing, clickjacking, and MIME sniffing attacks.

confidence.reason: Confirmed via curl and header configuration inspection.

title: Variable-Time Cryptographic Token Comparison Vulnerable to Timing Attack
description: Game session completion token verification used standard non-constant-time string comparison (!==), exposing the HMAC token to timing side-channel analysis.
root_cause: Direct !== comparison in session/finish/route.ts leaked execution time based on character match length.
intended_behavior: Cryptographic tokens must always be compared in constant time using crypto.timingSafeEqual.

trace.description: Direct string inequality comparison sessionToken !== expectedToken

evidence.description: Comparison uses JavaScript standard string comparison operator.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker sending high-volume requests measuring microsecond timing variations.
payloads: Iterative token candidates with incrementing byte prefixes.
instructions: Measure response latency to infer expected HMAC digest.
execution.observed_result: Varying response time according to matching prefix length.

remediation.strategy: Implement crypto.timingSafeEqual comparison via timingSafeTokenCompare utility.

likelihood.reason: Requires high-precision timing measurements across network.

impact.reason: Could allow forging valid session completion tokens.

confidence.reason: Source code inspection shows non-constant-time comparison.

title: Unauthenticated Orphaned Score API Granting Arbitrary XP and Coin Calculations
description: Legacy API route /api/scores/submit accepted unauthenticated score submissions and returned calculated XP and coin grants without session validation or proof of play.
root_cause: The route lacked authentication checks, HMAC session token requirements, or rate limiting.
intended_behavior: Score submission and reward calculations must be gated behind cryptographic session verification.

trace.description: Public POST handler accepting raw score payload
Returns calculated XP and coins without verifying gameplay session

evidence.description: Payload extracts score directly from request body without session token.

execution.attacker_perspective: An automated bot or script submitting fake scores.
execution.observed_result: API grants maximum base and bonus XP and coins.

remediation.strategy: Deprecate orphaned route and migrate all score tracking to authoritative cryptographic session pipeline.

likelihood.reason: Endpoint is publicly exposed and unauthenticated.

impact.reason: Allows reward harvesting and fake score calculations.

title: Unbounded In-Memory Rate Limiting Map Prone to Memory Exhaustion
description: In-memory rate limit maps in API routes accumulated IP keys indefinitely without background or size-based pruning, creating a memory leak risk under IP rotation attacks.
root_cause: rateLimitMap.set was called without evicting expired entries when map grew large.
intended_behavior: Rate limiting maps must prune expired timestamps and enforce a maximum size limit.

trace.description: New keys inserted without bounded size eviction

evidence.description: Map holds entries without a TTL eviction policy.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker rotating through synthetic X-Forwarded-For IP addresses.
payloads: Submissions using thousands of distinct IP headers.
instructions: Flood endpoint with different spoofed IP headers.
execution.observed_result: Node.js process heap memory increases monotonically.

remediation.strategy: Implement pruneRateLimitMap() with maximum size bounds and expired key deletion.

likelihood.reason: Requires high-volume targeted traffic with rotating IP addresses.

impact.reason: Causes gradual memory growth in serverless container.

confidence.reason: Verified by reviewing map lifecycle implementation.

title: Broken Object-Level Authorization in User Profile API
description: The user profile update API accepted a 'uid' parameter in the request body and updated that user's profile data without verifying that the caller was authenticated as that user.
root_cause: src/app/api/user/profile/route.ts updated profiles based solely on the unauthenticated body.uid parameter.
intended_behavior: The API must verify that the caller is authenticated and authorized to update the targeted user ID.

trace.description: Extracts uid directly from untrusted request body
Calls updateUserProfileData with target uid without caller verification
Firestore document updated with arbitrary profile changes

evidence.description: No session or authentication token check performed on uid parameter.

execution.attacker_perspective: A registered or unregistered remote attacker with knowledge of a victim's user ID.
instructions: Send PATCH request with arbitrary target uid.
execution.observed_result: Victim's profile display name, avatar, and bio are modified without authorization.

remediation.strategy: Verify caller identity via authentication headers and reject mismatched uid update requests.

likelihood.reason: Directly callable via standard HTTP PATCH.

impact.reason: Allows unauthorized modification of any user's profile, bio, and visual identity.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by code inspection and reproduction test.
